newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea vows to solve food crisis.
newsitem.headline: North Korea vows to solve food crisis.

text.p: North Korea on Wednesday singled out the nation's crippling food shortage as the key economic challenge in 1997.

"The central task of socialist economic construction this year is to....decisively solve the food problem," the nation's official newspapers said in a joint New Year editorial carried by the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) and monitored in Tokyo.
Reclusive North Korea has suffered famine after two consecutive years of flooding.

The United States pledged this week to ease a trade embargo against North Korea and give food aid after Pyongyang apologised for an incursion by one of its submarines into South Korean waters in September.
In the editorial, North Korea pledged to "radically improve" the people's standard of living, promote land administration and give primary importance to agriculture, light industry and foreign trade.

The editorial noted 1997 would mark the third anniversary of the death of long-time leader Kim Il-sung, but made no reference to the possibility of his son, Kim Jong-il, officially taking over Kim's role as president of the Stalinist state.
Analysts say Kim Jong-il is likely to take on the title of president this year after the three-year mourning period for his father ends in July.

The editorial urged the United States to "abandon its anachronistic policy of stifling Korea and show an affirmative response to our just proposal for the establishment of a new peace mechanism on the Korean Peninsula".
The two Koreas remain technically at war since their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce and not a peace treaty.
